images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the World Critic Model (WCM). Prior critic models are hindered by partial observability, and naïve multi-frame architectures remain inadequate due to sparse scalar supervision over high-dimensional observations. WCM proposes an end-to-end architecture that jointly predicts future and estimates value, effectively leveraging historical information. WCM achieves state-of-the-art performance in simulation and strong results in real-world RL training.

Figure 2:Overview of the World Critic Model (WCM) method. (a)Architecture.An observation encoder first maps individual images from the pastKKframes into sequential latent states. Concurrently, a predictor equipped with two decoder heads forecasts the next state and estimates the value respectively. (b)On-policy Pipeline: WCM estimates values from on-policy rollouts to compute GAE advantages for PPO/Flow-SDE updates. (c)Off-policy Pipeline: Unified data buffers (SFT + rollouts) are utilized to stably update both WCM and the policy via AWR/RECAP.
Figure 3:Graphical model of the POMDP formulation for VLA-RL. The solid circles represent observable quantities, while the hollow circles represent hidden states of the system.
Figure 4:Results on MetaWorld and CALVIN. We report success rate or average length with error bars.

Figure 5:Ablation study on critic architectures and observation history lengths. WCM achieves the highest success rates across all configurations. MLP denotes the baseline critic in PPO/Flow-SDE; ViT represents WCM without world prediction (λ=0\lambda=0), which has temporal modeling capability.

Figure 10:Throughput comparison of different policy variants across three tasks. Throughput is measured as the number of successful rollouts per hour. Bars represent mean values over four evaluation runs, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The SFT-only model shows low throughput across all tasks, while RECAP significantly improves throughput. Among the two RECAP variants, the WCM-based critic consistently outperforms the original Gemma-based critic.

header: Appendix EValue Curve Visualization of WCM

images.caption: Figure 12:WCM value curve in Maniskill.WCM exhibits strong discriminative capability between successful and failed trajectories. Because the motion planner in the simulation environment supplies ideal successful trajectories, the value estimates for successful trajectories are exceptionally smooth.

Figure 13:WCM value curve in the real world. Unlike simulation, real-world trajectories are not ideal: teleoperated trajectories are subject to various confounding factors, and both the environment and the camera introduce visual noise. Consequently, even successful trajectories show certain fluctuations. Nevertheless, the discriminability between successful and failed trajectories remains high.
